brand: A Day in the Life of a Flower Plaque Master

header.choose: Read the three orders, then choose today's job.

home.kicker: Hong Kong traditional flower plaques · Teaching simulation
home.title:
Three orders are
waiting for your reply.
home.lede: A higher quote does not guarantee a better profit. Size, deadline, staffing and transport all affect what remains.
home.disclaimer: All commercial figures are teaching assumptions. Energy and heat pressure are not medical assessments.

neighbourhood.title: Neighbourhood Tin Hau Festival
neighbourhood.description: Smaller scale and a looser deadline, but the income may not cover enough rent.

standard.title: Yuen Long Tin Hau Festival
standard.description: A more balanced mix of income and risk, typical for the workshop.

landmark.title: Large Festival Plaque
landmark.description: The highest quote, with greater size, overtime and installation risk.

decision.quoteBody: {{title}} | {{size}} ft | install in {{days}} days. A higher quote also raises expectations.

quote.title: What is this craft worth?
quote.body: A lower quote may win the order. A higher quote raises expectations.

low.title: Win-the-job price
low.note: Accepted immediately, with no extra fees allowed.

fair.title: Fair price
fair.note: A balance of specification and risk.

craft.title: Craft premium
craft.note: Accepted, but the client expects finer decoration.

craft.title: How will you make the plaque?
craft.body: Keeping every handmade process requires more material and time.

traditional.title: Fully handmade
traditional.note: Handwritten lettering and handmade decorations preserve the complete process.

hybrid.title: Hybrid production
hybrid.note: Print an outline, then colour by hand to balance time and craft.

prefab.title: Fast prefabrication
prefab.note: Lower cost, but some craft processes are no longer handmade.

staff.title: How many pairs of hands?
staff.body: More staff do not produce linear speed gains. Apprentices also need teaching time.

solo.title: Master works alone
solo.note: Helpers only arrive for installation; fatigue and delay risk rise.

skilled.title: Two skilled workers
skilled.note: A balanced option for time, quality and cost.

apprentice.title: Skilled worker + apprentice
apprentice.note: Teaching costs time now, but lets the next generation take part.

production.title: How will you use the last four days?
production.body: Working more today does not mean you will have the same energy tomorrow.

normal.title: Normal hours with rest
normal.note: Average speed, with the lowest rework risk.

overtime.title: Two hours overtime daily
overtime.note: More reliable progress, but the master's fair pay also rises.

simplify.title: Simplify two decorations
simplify.note: Protect the deadline, but reduce craft completeness.

changes.title: “Add six names and tweak it?”
changes.body: Only eighteen hours remain before loading. Changing text means layout, colouring and drying again.

free.title: Change it for free
free.note: The client is pleased, but the workshop absorbs the cost.

charge.title: Charge a change fee
charge.note: Put the extra work clearly into the contract.

decline.title: Politely decline
decline.note: No added cost, but the next order may be lost.

installation.title: 34°C. Finish before sunrise.
installation.body: This is a gamified heat-pressure scenario, not a medical assessment.

breaks.title: Rest ten minutes each hour
breaks.note: Reduce heat pressure and work at a steadier pace.

helpers.title: Hire two extra movers
helpers.note: Finish on time without sacrificing breaks.

rush.title: Keep rushing
rush.note: Energy collapses and parts need reinstalling.

outcome.intro: Understand the cost of this step before moving to the next day.
outcome.note: These changes are now in this run's ledger. All figures and scores are teaching assumptions.

labour.hint: Use the prompt to find the right action among the shuffled images.

bamboo.title: Complete one bamboo cross-joint
bamboo.body: Complete the four tying actions in order. In real work, every action needs accurate position and tension and is repeated across the plaque.
bamboo.completion: You completed one cross-joint. In real production, the master repeats similar work for days while keeping dimensions, tension and position accurate.

carry.title: Move six large parts into position
carry.body: Follow the installation sequence. Images show teamwork, environment and scale, not real weight, calorie use or a safety assessment.
carry.completion: All six parts are positioned. Real installation also includes loading, unloading, lifting, securing, wiring and dismantling, often before dawn or in heat and rain.

settlement.title:
The quote is not
what you keep.
settlement.intro: The client still owes {{amount}}. First calculate whether the full order made money, then look separately at cash on hand.
rows: Fair pay for the master's work ({{hours}} hours)

ending.loss: The plaque is finished, but the workshop paid for it.
ending.thin: The job is complete, with only a thin profit.
ending.nextAnnual: Zoom out to the full year

annual.contribution: Each order available for fixed costs
annual.impossibleNote: Each order fails to cover fixed costs
annual.caveat: This teaching scenario is based on your choices and does not represent real annual industry income.

settlement.history: How your choices built this ending
settlement.apprentice: Change role: live one month as an apprentice

questions: Would you enter a job that takes years to learn, long hours and a large workshop, but offers unstable income?
If young people do not enter the trade, is it only because they are not interested?
If society wants to preserve intangible cultural heritage, should one master bear the full cost?
reflection.note: There is no standard answer. Your choice stays only on this screen.
reflection.summaryTitle: Preserving a craft cannot depend on the master simply working harder.
reflection.summary: Rent support, fair procurement, training funding and stable orders are all part of preservation.

apprentice.kicker: Second perspective · You are a new apprentice · {{current}}/3
questions: There are only twelve workdays this month. How many do you accept?
Two installations run before dawn, with a HK$300 allowance each.
To work independently, the master recommends practice after work.
options: Keep time for school and rest; accept eight
Practise four unpaid hours each week
apprentice.resultTitle: Working hard does not guarantee a living.
apprentice.caveat: Day rate, workdays and living costs are teaching assumptions illustrating unstable income, not industry statistics.
